The Review Petitioner, in its rejoinder, has clarified that in para 16 of the present Review Petition, it has provided the details of the various pleadings filed before this Commission, whereby, the Review Petitioner has averred that it had inadvertently not claimed the cost of the 2 nd RUB in any earlier tariff petition, even though the 2 nd RUB was capitalized in 2014-15. This specific averment was somehow missed by this Commission. Furthermore, the Review Petitioner has stated that TANGEDCO in the main Petition has not even disputed the said claim and is raising the said contention for the first time, which is not permissible at this stage. 19. The Review Petitioner, in its rejoinder, has submitted that the Respondent TANGEDCO was a party in Petition No.293/GT/2014 filed by the Review Petitioner for the period 2014-19, whereby, the Commission vide its order dated 16.2.2017 allowed the water charges on an allocation basis, while rejecting the contention of the Respondent. It has also submitted that the principle applied in tariff cannot be changed at the truing up stage, in terms of the law declared by the Hon’ble Supreme Court, in BRPL v DERC & ors, wherein, it was held that the changing of rules/methodology used in the initial tariff determination exercise, would result in setting the tariff determination process at naught at the ‘truing-up’ stage. It is pertinent to mention that the Review Petitioner has sought the review of the methodology adopted by the Commission for the calculation of water charges based on actual allocation, instead of the same being on actual consumption as per agreement with the Orissa Irrigation Department. It is a settled position in terms of the judgment of the Hon’ble Supreme Court in Parsion Devi v Sumitra Devi (1997 8 SCC 715) that the review proceedings are not by way of an appeal and have to be strictly confined to the scope and ambit of Order 47 Rule 1 of CPC 1908 and that the judgment may be open to review, inter alia, if there is a mistake or an error apparent on the face of the record and that an error which is not self-evident and has to be detected by a process of reasoning can hardly be said to be an error apparent requiring the court to exercise its power of review. Accordingly, there is no error apparent on the face of the impugned order, and the prayer of the Review Petitioner for review of the impugned order on this ground is not maintainable. 27. In our view, the scope of the present review petition is limited to the issue raised by the Review Petitioner, and therefore, the counterclaims/reliefs sought by the Respondent cannot be considered. Even otherwise, we notice that the said issue raised by GRIDCO in Petition No. 16/RP/2023 has been examined and disposed of by the Commission vide its order dated 24.3.2025. 31.
